chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) or to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I postpone the fasting of three days of the month from summer to winter, for I find them easier for me then.' He said: 'Yes, but preserve their number.'
ai.seo_question: Can I postpone voluntary fasting days to a different season for ease?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal* highlights the jurisprudential flexibility (*rukhas*) in Shia tradition regarding voluntary fasting, specifically the three days of *Ayyam al-Beed* (the white days). The Imam’s permission to delay these fasts from the heat of summer to the ease of winter underscores the principle of balancing spiritual discipline with physical well-being, provided the total number of days is preserved. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on *wasatiyyah* (moderation) in acts of worship, ensuring they remain sustainable rather than burdensome.
